subject: Mosaic POC: shortfall top-up options and packaging question
messages:
From: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@mosaic.ai>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: Eli Navarro <eli@mgmt.mosaic.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick ask — 2 week cushion for POC vs seat swap

Hi Karthik,

Quick context: we're two-thirds through the Mosaic POC and engineering consumption is slightly higher than projected — estimated shortfall of ~18% on the timeboxed credits if we carry to the original end date (Sep 25).

We have two internal options on our side: 1) ask Redwood for a short 2-week top-up (timebox extension) to finish the final integration tests, or 2) repackage a small number of extra "developer seats" for the remainder and use them to queue more load (we can return unused seats if not consumed).

Can you outline how Redwood typically handles short, non-recurring top-ups for trials? Any precedent on a one-off grace window vs converting to seats for the last phase? Budget owner wants a quick answer today so we can make a call before our engineering sprint.

Thanks — appreciate a short note with options and the preferred path from Redwood.

—Sarah
Sarah Liu
Head of ML Ops, Mosaic AI
413-555-0192

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@mosaic.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 11 Sep 2026 11:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Quick ask — 2 week cushion for POC vs seat swap

Hi Sarah — thanks for the note and the clear choices. Short answer: both are doable, but there are trade-offs we should call out so you can align with procurement.

High-level options (quick):
- 2-week timebox top-up (recommended if you need deterministic wall-clock runway): add a one-off 14-day top-up that carries the existing credit bucket and preserves current throughput/latency profile. We typically price this as a fixed one-time top-up based on expected token consumption; for your 18% shortfall we'd suggest a 25% buffer to avoid another mid-run adjustment.
- Temporary seat allocation (recommended if you want flexible concurrency): provision N extra seats for 14 days; bills as pro-rated seat fees; unused seats cannot be converted back into token credits but can be de-provisioned mid-window.

I'll loop in Laura and Priyom for concrete numbers and a pricing snapshot. Attaching a short table with the two options and the rough cost delta.

If you want the cleanest conversion path back to production pricing after POC, the top-up keeps you on the same consumption model and avoids invoicing complexity. If your team is short on parallelism, seats give an immediate throughput boost.

Next steps: Laura, can you add a simple cost table and a one-line approval text that Mosaic can send to procurement? Priyom, flag any legal/license gating if we need a small addendum.

Karthik
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-3810

From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@mosaic.ai>, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 11 Sep 2026 14:02:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Quick ask — 2 week cushion for POC vs seat swap

Sarah / team — attaching the workbook with the numbers (mosaic-topup-options-tabulated.xlsx) and a draft mutual action paragraph you can paste into an approval email to procurement. Summary below: 

- Option A: 14-day timebox top-up (keeps token model): Estimated one-off fee $3,400 (includes 25% buffer). Pros: simplest amendment, no license change; Cons: billed as usage/top-up.
- Option B: 14-day temporary 4-seat burst (pro-rated): Estimated one-off fee $2,900. Pros: immediate concurrency boost; Cons: seats are billed pro-rata, unused seats not refundable and no automatic crediting back to tokens.

We recommend Option A for test-completion certainty. If procurement wants a slightly lower headline number and can accept potential unused seats, Option B is viable. 

Approval text (copy/paste):
"Redwood Inference to provide a one-time 14-day POC top-up for Mosaic AI (Deal DEAL-4827) per the attached cost table. Total amount not to exceed $3,400. Approval authorized by Sarah Liu (Mosaic AI)."

I'll wait for your direction and will prepare a formal addendum if you choose Option A.

-Laura
Sales Ops, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.ai

Karthik / Laura / Priyom — thanks for the clear options and the draft approval language. We've reviewed internally and procurement signs off on Option A (14-day timebox top-up) up to $3.4k. Please go ahead and send the addendum and invoice to procurement (procure@mosaic.ai). 

Also copying Hannah from our platform team — she may ask to reduce the buffer to 15% if you can give us near-real-time cost tracking. If you can accept a smaller buffer (and we monitor usage daily), we can drop the top-up to $2,900. Can you confirm whether we can do the 14-day top-up with a 15% buffer and daily burn telemetry for the team to monitor?

If yes, we'll confirm by EOD and you can send the addendum.

—Sarah
